what: The ignore rules, each annotated with the incident that motivated it, including the rule that keeps the third-party writing standard out of history.
why: A clone needs it to keep build products and campaign scratch out of the tree.

what: Maps seven author identities, including personal and cluster host addresses, onto one canonical contributor.
why: The export is one initial commit with no ancestry, so a mailmap has no history to fold and would only publish the address list.

what: Explains what the repository measures and how the stages connect, written for a physicist who has never used ROOT or PYTHIA.
why: It is the conceptual entry point a reader needs before rerunning anything.

what: Declares the associate-origin category contract the pair objects are written against.
why: The category axis of every published decomposition is defined by it.

what: The generated C++ view of the pair-file object contract, replacing three hand-maintained lists that had drifted apart.
why: It is a golden output and the closure counts derive from it.

what: The generated C++ view of the expanded pair registry, carrying its source digest.
why: It is a golden output the analysis, merge and closure all compile against.

what: The generated C++ view of the species ordinal table, so the ROOT-only analysis needs no JSON parser.
why: It is a golden output that puts the species axis into the compiled chain.

what: The index of every anchor directory, naming what each one anchors and whether its provenance is complete or incomplete.
why: It is the entry point to the provenance chain and states, per anchor, what can be verified and what cannot.

what: The manifest of the per-tune minimum-bias N_ch anchor, the evidence behind the multiplicity class definition and figure 3.
why: The paper-facing class translation table is recomputed from it rather than transcribed, which is a reproducibility claim.

what: The ROOT macro that dumps the minimum-bias N_ch distribution per tune into the committed CSV and ROOT pair.
why: It is the committed consumer of the anchor, so the class boundaries can be rederived rather than trusted.

what: The CLOSEPACKING minimum-bias charged-multiplicity distribution as text.
why: The published multiplicity class boundaries are derived from these distributions, so checking a boundary needs them.

what: The CLOSEPACKING minimum-bias charged-multiplicity histogram in ROOT form.
why: It is the binary the dump macro reads, and the CSV alone loses the binning the boundaries were cut on.

what: The JUNCTIONS minimum-bias charged-multiplicity distribution as text.
why: The published multiplicity class boundaries are derived from these distributions, so checking a boundary needs them.

what: The JUNCTIONS minimum-bias charged-multiplicity histogram in ROOT form.
why: It is the binary the dump macro reads, and the CSV alone loses the binning the boundaries were cut on.

what: The MONASH minimum-bias charged-multiplicity distribution as text.
why: The published multiplicity class boundaries are derived from these distributions, so checking a boundary needs them.

what: The MONASH minimum-bias charged-multiplicity histogram in ROOT form.
why: It is the binary the dump macro reads, and the CSV alone loses the binning the boundaries were cut on.

what: The run metadata of the minimum-bias generation: card, seed, event count and where it ran.
why: It is the provenance line that ties the committed distributions to a specific generator run.

what: The manifest of the two closure verdicts that gate the three-tune central table, and where their logs came from.
why: The brief rules boundary receipts PUBLIC: this is the record that the published table passed its gate.

what: The full CLOSEPACKING pair-block closure run log ending in its CANONICAL_PAIR_BLOCK_CLOSURE_PASS verdict.
why: Same role for the third tune's published column.

what: The full JUNCTIONS pair-block closure run log ending in the CANONICAL_PAIR_BLOCK_CLOSURE_PASS verdict.
why: It is the receipt behind a published column, and it existed only in cluster scratch before it was committed.

what: The waiter's own log, showing when each tune's blocks appeared and when each closure started.
why: It timestamps the gate runs whose verdicts the published table depends on.

what: The polling script that waited for both tunes' blocks to be promoted and then ran the closure gate on each.
why: It records how the two committed verdicts were actually produced, which is the invocation half of the receipt.

what: The single extracted CLOSEPACKING verdict line, separated from its log.
why: Same role for the third tune.

what: The single extracted JUNCTIONS verdict line, separated from its log.
why: It is the quotable form of the gate result the central table cites.

what: The driver that ran the deduplicating extractor over one tune's central merged directory.

what: The check that the deduplicated extraction reproduces the predicted E5 totals rather than merely differing from the replicated one.

what: The per-category weights of the quarantined first anchor extraction.

what: The per-observable weights of the quarantined first anchor extraction.

what: The per-species weights of the quarantined first anchor extraction.

what: The build and run manifest of the extended probe, with the digests of the binary and its inputs.

what: The original PYTHIA-linked decay probe output: 202 species, dominant channel only.
